description: We are a passionate team of students and tech enthusiasts brought together by our curiosity about space and our love for solving real-world problems. Our goal is to build a creative, practical solution using NASA’s open data, combining ideas from technology, design, and science. We believe that teamwork, learning, and experimentation are the keys to innovation, and we’re excited to turn our ideas into something that can make a real impact. Let’s explore, build, and reach for the stars together!
summary:
Celestia is an interactive chatbot that explains NASA’s spacecraft and discoveries directly to children aged 6-12. Inspired by Voyager’s journey and the way it made humanity look up, we asked: how can children feel that same wonder today?

Big discoveries can feel distant to young learners, and long explanations lose their attention. Celestia solves this with simple language, short exchanges, and conversation-led exploration. A child scans a QR code, meets Celestia, and keeps exploring through a loop of inviting prompts, friendly explanations, and bite-sized answers.

Celestia is scripted by design, not open-ended AI. Every response is prepared in advance and can be checked against trusted NASA sources, giving parents and educators confidence in what children receive.

This matters because early curiosity shapes future interest in science, technology, and exploration. Our vision is to place Celestia QR codes inside children’s science books, giving every child a trusted, playful starting point for space learning. One scan can turn a page into a guided moment of discovery.
details:
What it does and how it works
Celestia is a conversational guide that introduces children to NASA’s spacecraft and discoveries, beginning with Voyager. The child meets Celestia, asks questions or chooses from suggested prompts, and receives short, friendly answers. Each exchange follows a simple loop: Invite, Explain, Continue. Prompts invite the next question, explanations turn complex ideas into approachable ones, and each reply is short enough to hold a child’s attention. Celestia runs on a prepared script rather than open-ended AI, so every answer is written in advance and can be checked against trusted NASA sources.

Benefits
Children get space facts that feel playful and easy to understand instead of distant or difficult. Parents and educators get content that is predictable, reviewable, and safe by default. Because every answer is traceable to NASA sources, accuracy and trust are built in.

Intended impact
We want space curiosity to become part of growing up. Celestia aims to give every child a trusted starting point for learning about space and to build early foundations for science, technology, and exploration. As a future direction, we see a path to reach children through printed science books using QR codes, so a page can become a guided moment of exploration.

NASA resources: Voyager mission information and NASA imagery, including the Golden Record. No special hardware is needed beyond a phone, tablet, or computer.

Creativity
Celestia connects a historic NASA story to today’s children, using the Golden Record as an emotional hook. Its scripted design is a deliberate creative choice, treating safety and trust as part of the concept. It also replaces lecture-style explanations with a short, playful conversation in a child’s own language.

Factors our team considered
We considered the audience (language and tone for ages 6-12), attention span (short exchanges), safety and trust (a verifiable script instead of unpredictable AI), accuracy (answers grounded in NASA sources), and scalability (the format can expand to other missions and new distribution channels).
